assertion: PPSL estimates the Department of Education is falsely reporting $4.6 billion in canceled debt to credit agencies, impacting more than 300,000 borrowers.

sources.title: PPSL press release: Student Borrowers Sue Education Department for Reporting Cancelled Loans as Debt
CNBC: Student loan borrowers sue over credit reports listing forgiven debt

reason: The article accurately attributes this figure to PPSL as an estimate rather than presenting it as fact — confirmed by a word-for-word match against PPSL's own press release ('PPSL estimates, based on publicly available data...'). But whether the $4.6B/300,000 figure itself is ACCURATE cannot be independently checked: PPSL discloses no methodology, the Department of Education has not confirmed or disputed it, and no public Federal Student Aid dataset exists to recompute it independently. This is graded 'not checkable here' as to the estimate's own accuracy — the attribution itself is accurate (see narrative).

assertion: A class action lawsuit claims borrowers with forgiven loans are still being reported as delinquent to credit bureaus, harming their credit.
independent_value: PPSL press release: 'the Department continues to furnish information to Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion showing cancelled loans as outstanding debt.' CNBC independently reports the same, naming the same three bureaus.

sources.title: PPSL complaint PDF: Woods et al. v. United States Department of Education

reason: Direct textual match to the primary-source press release and complaint, independently corroborated by CNBC the same day.

assertion: These borrowers were among the 1.5 million borrowers who, from 2022 to 2025, had $23.4 billion in loans forgiven through the Department of Education group discharge program for those who attended a college that allegedly engaged in misconduct. Borrowers were told the relief was automatic and they did not have to take any further action.
independent_value: PPSL press release: 'Between April 2022 and January 2025, the Department announced final group discharges covering more than 1.5 million borrowers and $23.4 billion in loans... The Department told eligible borrowers that the relief was automatic, that they had no obligation to make additional payments, and that they did not need to take further action.'
reason: Verbatim match to the primary-source press release on dates, dollar figure, borrower count, and the 'automatic relief, no action needed' representation to borrowers.

assertion: The Department of Education declined to comment on the case Thursday.
independent_value: CNBC (same day): 'The Education Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.' Benzinga reported the same for its own outreach.
reason: Two independent outlets contacting DOE the same day both report no response, consistent with the article's characterization.
